**Root cause:** The installed dependency (`urllib3==2.0.7`, pulled in through `requests`) changed how `HTTPConnectionPool._make_request` drives connections. urllib3 2.x now always calls:

```python
conn.request(method, url, body=..., headers=..., chunked=...,
             preload_content=..., decode_content=..., enforce_content_length=...)
```

Those keyword arguments (notably `chunked`) are only accepted by `urllib3.connection.HTTPConnection`, whose `request()` signature implements chunked framing and response-option handling. Docker's `UnixHTTPConnection` was subclassing plain `http.client.HTTPConnection` (via `httplib`), whose `request()` rejects `chunked`, hence the `TypeError`.

**Fix:** In `docker/transport/unixconn.py`, I changed `UnixHTTPConnection` to subclass `urllib3.connection.HTTPConnection` instead of `httplib.HTTPConnection`. The custom `connect()` (which plugs in a `AF_UNIX` socket) and `response_class()` overrides are preserved, so the unix-socket path now flows through urllib3 2.x's request/getresponse machinery — matching how the TCP adapter already works and how the rest of the client code (`response.raw._fp`, chunked stream reading, etc.) expects responses to be shaped.
